items.stem: How is the Well-Architected Framework best used over a system's life?

options.text: As an ongoing, repeated review practice as the workload evolves
options.rationale: Correct: Well-Architected is iterative and revisited as the system changes.

options.text: As a one-time certification completed before launch
options.rationale: It is not a one-time check; architectures change and should be re-reviewed.

options.text: As a replacement for monitoring and operations
options.rationale: It complements, not replaces, operational practices.

options.text: As a billing feature that reduces cost automatically
options.rationale: It is a review framework, not an automatic cost reducer.

items.explanation: Correct: Well-Architected is an ongoing review practice, not a one-time event.

items.stem: Which TWO align with the Reliability pillar? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: multi-AZ deployment removes a single-AZ point of failure.

options.text: Define recovery objectives (RTO/RPO) and test failover
options.rationale: Correct: defining and testing recovery targets is core to reliability.

options.text: Run everything in one AZ to simplify networking
options.rationale: A single AZ is a reliability risk, not a reliability practice.

options.text: Skip backups to save storage cost

items.explanation: Correct: multi-AZ deployment and tested recovery objectives both support reliability.

items.stem: Which practice best reflects the Security pillar's principle of least privilege?

options.text: Grant each identity only the permissions its task requires
options.rationale: Correct: least privilege limits permissions to what is needed.

options.text: Give all users administrator access for convenience
options.rationale: Blanket admin access violates least privilege.

options.text: Share one root account among the team
options.rationale: Sharing root is a serious security anti-pattern.
Disabling logging weakens detection, not a security practice.

items.explanation: Correct: granting only required permissions is least privilege.
